def-gibbs-full-conditional-kernel:
## Definition

Let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set, let $(S_i,\mathcal S_i)_{i\in I}$ be measurable spaces, set $S=\prod_{i\in I}S_i$ with its finite product sigma-algebra, and let $\pi$ be a probability measure on $S$. For a nonempty block $B\subseteq I$, write $S_B=\prod_{i\in B}S_i$, $S_{-B}=\prod_{i\in I\setminus B}S_i$, let $p_{-B}:S\to S_{-B}$ be the coordinate projection, and define $\pi_{-B}(D):=\pi(p_{-B}^{-1}(D))$ for measurable $D\subseteq S_{-B}$.

Products and product sigma-algebras use the empty-product convention in [[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]: if $B=I$, then $S_{-B}$ is the one-point space $\{()\}$ with its trivial sigma-algebra.

A **proper full conditional kernel** for block $B$ is a supplied probability kernel $K_B:S_{-B}\to S_B$ such that for every product-measurable $C\subseteq S$ and every measurable $D\subseteq S_{-B}$,
$$
\pi\bigl(C\cap p_{-B}^{-1}(D)\bigr)=\int_D K_B(z,C_z)\,\pi_{-B}(dz),\qquad C_z:=\{u\in S_B:\operatorname{splice}_B(z,u)\in C\}.
$$
Here $\operatorname{splice}_B(z,u)$ is the unique state whose coordinates on $I\setminus B$ are $z$ and whose coordinates on $B$ are $u$. This is the event-identity definition of a regular conditional distribution of the block given the retained coordinates, with every kernel section a probability measure at every $z$. It makes no existence claim; the A-page density corollary gives one sufficient case.
def-gibbs-reversibility-for-a-markov-ker:
## Definition

Let $P$ be a probability kernel on $(S,\mathcal S)$ and let $\pi$ be a probability measure on that space. The kernel $P$ is **reversible with respect to $\pi$**, or satisfies **detailed balance**, when
$$
\int_A P(x,C)\,\pi(dx)=\int_C P(y,A)\,\pi(dy)\qquad(A,C\in\mathcal S).
$$
This is the symmetry of the two-time transition flow $\pi(dx)P(x,dy)$, stated through its values on measurable rectangles. The definition is for a general measurable state space and makes no irreducibility, uniqueness, or convergence assertion. Invariance means $\int P(x,A)\,\pi(dx)=\pi(A)$ for every $A\in\mathcal S$, as in [[def-invariant-and-stationary-distribution-for-a-markov-kernel]].
def-finite-markov-chain-reducible:
## Definition

Let $E$ be a finite nonempty state space and $p$ a transition matrix on $E$. A subset $C\subseteq E$ is **closed** when $\sum_{y\in C}p(x,y)=1$ for every $x\in C$. The finite chain is **reducible** when it has a nonempty proper closed subset. This definition is the only reducibility convention used by the finite-support example on this page.
cor-gibbs-density-formula-supplies-full-:
## Statement

Let $(S_B,\mathcal S_B,\mu)$ and $(S_{-B},\mathcal S_{-B},\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure spaces. Suppose a probability law $\pi$ on their product has a nonnegative product-measurable density $p(u,z)$ with respect to $\mu\times\nu$. Fix a supplied probability measure $\rho$ on $S_B$ and put
$$m(z)=\int_{S_B}p(u,z)\,\mu(du),\qquad D=\{z:0<m(z)<\infty\}.$$
Then
$$K_B(z,A)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle \frac{\int_Ap(u,z)\,\mu(du)}{m(z)},&z\in D,\\[4pt]\rho(A),&z\notin D,\end{cases}$$
is a proper full conditional kernel for $\pi$.
alg-gibbs-block-update:
## Definition

**Inputs:** The finite product state space and target law from [[def-gibbs-full-conditional-kernel]], a nonempty block $B$, its supplied proper full conditional kernel $K_B$, and a current state $x\in S$.

**Output:** A new state $x'\in S$ whose retained coordinates equal $x_{-B}$ and whose updated block is sampled from $K_B(x_{-B},\cdot)$.

The transition kernel is
$$P_B(x,C)=\int_{S_B}\mathbf1_C\!\left(\operatorname{splice}_B(x_{-B},u)\right)K_B(x_{-B},du),\qquad C\in\mathcal S.$$
Operationally, retain every coordinate outside $B$, draw $u$ from the full conditional kernel at the retained value, and replace the coordinates in $B$ by $u$. The finite product sigma-algebra makes the splice map measurable; the kernel-integral theorem makes the displayed evaluation measurable in $x$. The well-definedness result is [[lem-gibbs-block-update-is-a-probability-kernel]].
cor-bivariate-normal-full-conditional-ke:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $m_X,m_Y\in\mathbb R$, let $\sigma_X,\sigma_Y>0$, and let $-1<r<1$. Put
$$\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_X^2&r\sigma_X\sigma_Y\\r\sigma_X\sigma_Y&\sigma_Y^2\end{pmatrix},\qquad \pi=N_2\bigl((m_X,m_Y),\Sigma\bigr).$$
Then proper full conditional kernels of $X$ given $Y=y$ and of $Y$ given $X=x$, at every real conditioning value, are
$$X\mid Y=y\sim N\!\left(m_X+r\frac{\sigma_X}{\sigma_Y}(y-m_Y),\,\sigma_X^2(1-r^2)\right),\qquad Y\mid X=x\sim N\!\left(m_Y+r\frac{\sigma_Y}{\sigma_X}(x-m_X),\,\sigma_Y^2(1-r^2)\right).$$
Both conditional variances are strictly positive. The singular cases $|r|=1$ are not included.
lem-gibbs-block-update-is-a-probability-:
## Statement

For every supplied proper full conditional kernel, the transition formula in [[alg-gibbs-block-update]] defines a probability kernel on the full product state space.
alg-gibbs-scan-schemes:
## Definition

**Inputs:** An integer $m\ge1$, a list of nonempty blocks $B_1,\ldots,B_m$, their exact block-update kernels $P_1,\ldots,P_m$ from [[alg-gibbs-block-update]], and, for random scan, fixed weights $w_j\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^m w_j=1$.

**Random scan:** At each update choose index $j$ with probability $w_j$ and apply $P_j$. Its one-update kernel is
$$P_{\rm rand}(x,A)=\sum_{j=1}^m w_jP_j(x,A).$$
Uniform random scan is the special case $w_j=1/m$.

**Systematic scan:** Apply $P_1$, then $P_2$, through $P_m$, and repeat that fixed order. For kernels, $P_1\cdots P_m$ means chronological composition: apply $P_1$ first and $P_m$ last, as in [[def-composition-of-probability-kernels]]. The state observed after each single update has the phase-indexed sequence of kernels $P_1,\ldots,P_m,P_1,\ldots$ and is generally time-inhomogeneous; the state observed only at full-sweep boundaries is a homogeneous chain with kernel $P_1\cdots P_m$. The scan procedures are well-defined probability kernels by [[lem-gibbs-scan-schemes-are-probability-kernels]].
lem-gibbs-block-refresh-is-conditionally:
## Statement

Assume AC for the conditional-expectation class convention in [[def-conditional-independence-given-a-sigma-algebra]]. Let $X=(U,Z)$ have law $\pi$, where $U$ is the block $B$ and $Z$ is the retained coordinate. Update once using [[alg-gibbs-block-update]], and write $V$ for the refreshed block. Under the resulting joint law of $(U,Z,V)$,
$$U\perp\!\!\!\perp V\mid\sigma(Z).$$
Both $U$ and $V$ have conditional law $K_B(Z,\cdot)$ given $Z$.
lem-gibbs-block-update-is-reversible-and:
## Statement

Let $\pi$ be a probability on a finite product state space and let $K_B$ be a supplied proper full conditional kernel for a nonempty block $B$. The exact block-update kernel $P_B$ of [[alg-gibbs-block-update]] is reversible with respect to $\pi$ and leaves $\pi$ invariant.
lem-gibbs-scan-schemes-are-probability-k:
## Statement

For an integer $m\ge1$, a list of exact Gibbs block-update probability kernels $P_1,\ldots,P_m$, and supplied weights $w_j\ge0$ summing to one, both scan procedures of [[alg-gibbs-scan-schemes]] define probability kernels.
thm-random-scan-gibbs-is-reversible-and-:
## Statement

Let $m\ge1$, let $P_1,\ldots,P_m$ be exact block-update kernels for one target probability $\pi$, and let $w_j\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^m w_j=1$. Then $P_{\rm rand}=\sum_{j=1}^m w_jP_j$ is reversible with respect to $\pi$ and leaves $\pi$ invariant. No irreducibility or convergence conclusion follows from this statement.
thm-systematic-gibbs-sweep-preserves-tar:
## Statement

Let $m\ge1$ and let $P_1,\ldots,P_m$ be exact block-update kernels for the same target probability $\pi$. Under the chronological composition convention of [[def-composition-of-probability-kernels]], the systematic full-sweep kernel $P_1\cdots P_m$ leaves $\pi$ invariant. It need not be reversible.
